articles.title: 'Avatar: La Leyenda de Aang' se expande con una nueva serie, 'Avatar: Seven Havens', que ya tiene tráiler y fecha de estreno
articles.text:
La franquicia de Avatar: La Leyenda de Aang estrenará este mismo 2026 una nueva serie, Avatar: Seven Havens. Será el tercer proyecto televisivo de la saga (el cuarto si sumamos el remake live-action de Netflix). Y durante el panel de la San Diego Comic Con dedicado a la inminente película Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender se ha dejado un primer vistazo a este nuevo título que servirá de secuela para los anteriores.
Avatar: Seven Havens nos presentará a la joven Pavi, una maestra de la Tierra que descubrirá que es la siguiente reencarnación del Avatar después de Aang y Korra. La pequeña vive en la ciudad de Allura, azotada por el viento y la arena. Pero su mundo es muy diferente a los de sus predecesores. Ahora se divide en "Siete Paraísos" y, por desgracia, ha sido destrozado por un cataclismo devastador.
En esta peligrosa época, de hecho, la humanidad no ve al Avatar como el salvador que trae el equilibrio y la paz. Por el contrario, el Avatar es visto como el destructor de la humanidad. Perseguida tanto por enemigos humanos como espirituales, Pavi y su gemela, a la que no veía desde hacía mucho tiempo, deben desentrañar sus misteriosos orígenes y salvar los Siete Paraísos antes de que se derrumben los últimos bastiones de la civilización.
Mira el tráiler de Avatar: Seven Havens
Además del tráiler, el panel de la San Diego Comic Con también nos ha dejado la esperada fecha de estreno de Avatar: Seven Havens, que llegará a Paramount+ el 9 de octubre de este 2026. Esta fecha es ya conocida por los fans de la franquicia. Y es que era la elegida para el estreno de la película Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender. Sin embargo, el filme se filtró online al completo por error, lo que llevó al estudio a adelantar su estreno al 25 de julio. Así las cosas, ahora reaprovechan la fecha original para su nueva serie.
Además, un dato que sí sorprenderá a los fans es que los 26 episodios de Avatar: Seven Havens, divididos en dos "libros", se estrenarán de manera simultánea el mismo día. Tanto Avatar: La Leyenda de Aang (2005) como Avatar: La Leyenda de Korra (2012) se estrenaron en su día de manera semanal en televisión. Pero al dar el salto con el streaming, esto cambia para siempre.

articles.title: Pascal Siakam’s edtech accelerator awards three startups with $50,000 | BetaKit
articles.text:
NBA champion “Spicy P” was back in Toronto this week to name the prizewinners of his edtech accelerator program.
The news: The Siakam EdTech Engine—an edtech accelerator run by former Toronto Raptor Pascal Siakam’s foundation and Toronto Metropolitan University’s DMZ—hosted its demo day on Tuesday, awarding $50,000 in total grants to three startups that pitched their solutions to improve educational technology.
AI-powered assessment platform Classwise won the top prize, followed by tailored learning platform Training Ground.ai and professional networking service CoLab Education.
From the podium: In an interview with francophone radio station Choq FM after the event, Siakam hinted that he hopes the program continues to expand.
“I hope it’ll continue to grow, so we can have more prizes, and these companies can come and earn a little more,” Siakam said in French remarks that BetaKit has translated. “In the end, I hope that their impact will be felt throughout the community, and that the youth will feel it too.”
Following the pass: Siakam was drafted by and played seven and a half seasons for the Toronto Raptors, including their 2019 championship win. Though he was traded to the Indiana Pacers in 2024—and boasted an average of 24 points and 6.6 rebounds per game last season—he has continued to support his former city.
Launched in February 2025, the 12-week edtech accelerator in Toronto is a collaboration between PS43, a not-for-profit founded by the champion power forward, and DMZ. According to the website, participating startups are connected with industry and education leaders, and get to pilot their tech solutions with school boards, teachers, and students.
Classwise founder Derah Onuorah said in a statement to BetaKit that since building in edtech is “notoriously difficult,” working alongside other founders in the same space was a big motivator to keep going.
Final score: Through PS43, Siakam’s philanthropic education work extends beyond the city of Toronto, especially now that he plays for the Pacers. In December, the foundation announced it was providing Indiana Math and Science Academy West with two new digital education platforms—one for cyber safety and an AI-powered reading tutor.
Feature image courtesy DMZ.

articles.title: DAC 2026: DIY AI Is Now in Vogue; Users Are Not Waiting - EE Times
articles.text:
When my friend Simon Davidmann, whose framework anchored Part 1 of this series, laid out his agentic AI argument in recent months, one observation got less attention than his band-aid-versus-reset headline, yet it deserves more: The customers are doing it themselves. Hyperscalers and semiconductor houses are not waiting for vendors to ship finished AI products. They are building their own orchestration, their own agents, and their own models, on top of the simulation, formal, implementation, and signoff engines they already license. The EDA tools become engines; the intelligence layer above them increasingly belongs to the user.
As Simon pointed out, Samsung, Nvidia, and their peers are assembling internal AI stacks that treat vendor tools as engines beneath a domain-specific intelligence layer. But he attached a barbed caveat: Because that work stays behind corporate firewalls, it is “effective and myopic at the same time.” Each giant rebuilds similar integrations in private; the lessons never propagate to the rest of the industry—and, worse for the rest of us, the giants get to learn from all their own data, something those outside the walls can only wish for. That is Davidmann’s Dilemma from Part 1 in its purest form: every player acting rationally and the ecosystem collectively worse off for it.
If you want evidence that DIY AI is now mainstream practice rather than hyperscaler exotica—and, contra Simon’s caveat, that at least some of the lessons are starting to propagate in public—the DAC 2026 Engineering Track is the closest thing we have to proof. An honest qualifier belongs here: The most secretive giants still are not presenting—you will not find Nvidia, Meta, or OpenAI walking through their internal design-AI stacks, and some of the industry’s most advanced users treat their flows as IP and stay home entirely. What the Track shows is the visible part of the iceberg. But the visible part has grown remarkably.
The Engineering Track is DAC’s user conference within the conference—working engineers presenting deployed results, peer-reviewed by other engineers—and this year, it reads like a census of do-it-yourself AI. What follows is my tour of the DIY AI wave, followed by its deliberate juxtaposition: users adopting the vendors’ AI, with equally concrete numbers. Both are true simultaneously, and the tension between them is exactly where Simon’s framework earns its keep.
Exhibit A: Samsung teaches an RL agent to tune an SoC
Start with the presentation I would use to explain the entire trend to a skeptic: On Monday morning, Samsung Electronics engineers Hyungtae Park, Rira Oh, Sanggu Kim, Hyunjae Woo, and Youngsik Kim present “Adaptive QoS Optimization for SoC Performance Enhancement Using Dueling Double Deep Q-Networks.” The problem: Modern SoCs expose a thicket of quality-of-service knobs—arbitration, priorities, bandwidth allocations across many masters—and manually tuning them across varying scenarios has become intractable. Samsung’s answer: Build an execution environment that runs the SoC pre-silicon—think emulation—and set a reinforcement-learning (RL) agent loose in it. The agent—Deep Q-Networks with dueling and double-DQN enhancements, prioritized experience replay, the full modern RL toolkit—explores the design space against reward functions built on throughput, latency, and power and discovers QoS settings that significantly outperform manual methods.
Notice the architecture of the achievement—and notice, per Part 1’s model-spectrum musing, that there is no LLM in sight: This is a user-trained optimization model, not a wrapped chatbot. The execution infrastructure that makes the exploration trustworthy comes from the EDA world; the intelligence that exploits it is Samsung’s own, purpose-built for Samsung’s architectures and Samsung’s performance targets for what they call “System Performance Verification.” That division of labor—vendor engines below, user intelligence above—is Simon’s observation rendered as a methodology paper, and it repeats across the track.
The DIY AI census
IBM turns agents loose on verification debug—and on tool development itself. In IBM Z hardware verification, agentic flows now automate failure triage and root-cause analysis, integrating design specifications, HDL, waveforms, coverage data, and prior issues through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, with customized agents extracting cone-of-influence logic and correlating transactions—reporting an estimated 15% to 40% reduction in manual effort on one of the most expertise-hungry tasks in the flow.
A second IBM paper goes a level more meta: an agentic framework that generates EDA utilities themselves from user specifications using reusable MCP building blocks, reducing one structural-verification tool’s development from an estimated four person-weeks to under 30 minutes. Note MCP appearing twice: The connective-tissue standard from Part 1’s data-and-glue layer (where Perforce pairs it with RAG for design-data context) is showing up in user methodology papers barely a year after entering the conversation. The connective tissue is arriving. And it raises a question Simon put to me directly, worth carrying into Tuesday’s Build-versus-Buy panel: Why are the big EDA vendors not shipping these utilities themselves—and why are users such as IBM building rather than buying from the startups next door?
An on-premises LLM babysits emulation regressions
A flagship-SoC team from Samsung presents an unattended software-testing framework for pre-silicon emulation that pairs fast-boot virtualization with an on-premises LLM that reads kernel panics and decides: genuine software bug or non-critical bring-up artifact? The detail to savor is “on-premises”—the confidentiality requirements of semiconductor design mean the user’s DIY AI runs inside the user’s walls, on top of the vendor’s emulation platform. Another team presents an on-premises, multi-agent “Team of Experts” pipeline—a classifier agent routing to specialized sub-agents for UVM code generation, log parsing, and specification retrieval across JEDEC, LPDDR, and HBM documents—built with RAG and finetuning precisely so that no design data leaves the building.
The knowledge layer gets formalized
A Samsung team presents an ontology-driven knowledge graph that transforms hundreds of pages of interlinked design documents into a queryable graph feeding a Graph-RAG chatbot—the specification-engineering thread from Part 1’s front-end stage, implemented by users for users. In the POWER processor verification environment, ML-driven analysis correlates test components with coverage events and composes “super-tests” that make up 86% of recommended test cases for hard-to-hit scenarios.
Implementation and analog join in
Texas Instruments describes a deep-RL analog sizing tool—with custom reward shaping, optimizing across all PVT and Monte Carlo corners—deployed at scale with over 100 circuits optimized to signoff quality. An automotive SoC team from Renesas presents a Random Forest framework predicting die size from design specifications with R2 up to 0.95 across 1,800 RTL modules. On the Gladiator stage, a team from Samsung uses LLMs to interpret netlists and cluster DRAM peripheral cells for placement—expert structural knowledge written as natural-language prompts rather than rule-based code—cutting design-rule violations by 80.6%, while Samsung’s Sungsu Byun applies gradient-boosted models to switch-cell optimization against RedHawk-reported voltage variation. A neuro-symbolic framework presented by Cadence called Auto-Chk compiles natural-language signoff intent into deterministic checkers—120+ checklist items in production, 20× faster checker development. Even formal verification gets the treatment: AI-generated “helper” invariants converting bounded proofs into full closure. And one paper turns AI on the infrastructure itself, using graph neural networks and RL to forecast EDA compute needs, cutting cloud overprovisioning by 60% to 80%.
Add it up, and the pattern is unmistakable: RL agents, on-prem LLMs, knowledge graphs, multi-agent pipelines, neuro-symbolic compilers—built by users, running on vendor engines, presented with deployment numbers rather than aspirations. Hold each one up to Davidmann’s Test, and the census gets even more interesting: Most of this speeds up what their teams already verified—dramatically, honestly, and with numbers. A few—the invariants that convert bounded proofs into full closure, the QoS exploration no human team could have swept—edge toward changing what can be verified at all.
The juxtaposition: vendor AI, adopted and audited
Now let’s look at the other half of the picture, because the same Track that documents the DIY AI wave also documents users adopting vendor AI—and, in the best Engineering Track tradition, auditing it in public.
A user methodology paper on Cadence Voltus InsightAI examines AI-driven power-grid reinforcement for IR closure—and does something refreshingly honest: It presents a detailed design-impact analysis for working with the tool’s capabilities and around its limitations. That sentence is the Engineering Track’s entire value proposition in miniature. Broadcom’s APD AI team and Synopsys’s RedHawk-ET team jointly present an early 3DIC thermal flow, correlated to silicon within 3°C (Part 3 returns to it)—vendor AI and user expertise co-developed rather than bought off the shelf. Intel presents its library QA framework built on Siemens’s Solido Crosscheck, native checks fine-tuned alongside custom ones. An AI-driven thermal-aware placement methodology explores hundreds of constrained scenarios for 3D chiplet stacks. And in the special sessions, Sandisk’s Mariana Shenker shows production AI workflows for specification-driven development—the user-experience counterpart to the “Spec-Tacular!” session’s startup pitches.
So which is it: users building their own or users adopting the vendors’? The Track’s answer is both, sorted by where the intelligence needs to live. Where the problem is deeply proprietary—an SoC’s QoS behavior, a company’s debug tribal knowledge, confidential failure logs—the AI is homegrown and on-premises, with vendor engines supplying the physics and the simulation truth underneath. Where the problem is common to everyone—IR closure, library QA, thermal analysis—vendor AI embedded in the platforms wins on economics. The boundary between those two zones is, I suspect, where the next five years of EDA business models get decided. Simon’s holistic reset, if it comes, will have to serve both sides of that line; Monday’s DAC Pavilion panel “Agentic AI in EDA: Who’s in Control?” and Tuesday’s “Build vs Buy: Who Owns the Intelligence Behind Tomorrow’s Chips?” put that exact question on stage, and Simon himself joins Wednesday’s exhibitor forum panel, “Harnessing AI for SoC Verification: Disruptive or Collaborative?”—the perfect closing argument for this article’s thesis, argued live.
For the startup-side complement to these user stories, Monday’s Veriest-hosted exhibitor forum session, “Beyond the Hype: Innovation in AI for Chip Design and Verification,” showcases what the agentic layer from Part 1’s landscape is building for exactly these users.
The itinerary, complete
Three parts, one arc: Part 1, the landscape of who; Part 2, the users quietly building their own intelligence on the industry’s engines; and Part 3, the sessions on creating AI chips—the end product this whole industry exists for.
And if Part 1’s Expedia comparison did not convince you, here is a culinary one: Think of DAC Explorer as the conference’s AI sous-chef. Hand it the ingredients you fancy: say, a base of RL, some on-premises LLMs, and a pinch of MCP, and it finds the recipe—a personalized schedule of sessions, plated and ready to export. No reservations are required, although seats at the popular sessions do go fast.
Registration is at dac.com, and every session mentioned here is in the official DAC 2026 program. See you in Long Beach.
Frank Schirrmeister writes about semiconductors, EDA, and system design. He serves as program chair of the DAC Engineering Track; this series is written in that capacity, not on behalf of his employer, Synopsys. Opinions are his own.

articles.title: Un éclair frappe une fusée chinoise en plein vol
articles.text:
C’est une image impressionnante que le compte CNSPACE a mise en lumière ce 23 juillet 2026 sur le réseau social X. En effet, c’était aujourd’hui qu’était organisé le décollage de la fusée Longue Marche 3B depuis la base de lancement de Xichang, dans la province du Sichuan (sud-ouest de la Chine). Une mission de routine sur le papier, qui consistait simplement à envoyer sur orbite le satellite Tianlian-2-06.
Sauf que l’ascension du lanceur n’a pas été de tout repos. Comme on peut le voir sur l’extrait vidéo partagé par CNSPACE, un compte spécialisé dans le suivi du programme spatial chinois, la fusée a été frappée par un éclair lors de sa montée dans l’atmosphère. Et cela, tout juste trente secondes après le décollage.
Un événement spectaculaire qui ne semble pas avoir empêché la mission d’aller à son terme : « Jeudi, la Chine a mis en orbite avec succès un nouveau satellite de relais de données depuis le centre de lancement de Xichang », a résumé Xinhua, une agence de presse rattachée à l’administration centrale. Le satellite a bien atteint l’orbite attendue, selon Xinhua.
Cette affaire, visiblement sans conséquence, rappelle une réalité physique bien connue des ingénieurs : en matière de vol spatial, la météo n’est jamais un paramètre secondaire. Reporter un lancement parce que le ciel est menaçant n’est aucunement une coquetterie pour s’assurer de jolies photos sur les réseaux sociaux. Il y a des enjeux de sécurité.
La fusée peut déclencher la foudre
Un lanceur ne subit pas forcément les éléments de manière passive. Il peut tout à fait déclencher l’éclair qui va le frapper.
En traversant l’atmosphère, il recrache au passage un long panache de gaz chauds ionisés. Combinée à la structure métallique de l’engin, cette traînée de combustion crée un canal conducteur entre le sol et les charges électriques accumulées dans l’atmosphère.
C’est précisément ce que vise la règle sur les nuages de type cumulus. Même en l’absence totale d’orage ou d’activité électrique décelable, le simple fait pour une fusée de traverser un cumulus peut suffire à déclencher un éclair de toutes pièces.
De la frayeur d’Apollo 12 au drame d’Atlas-Centaur
L’histoire de la conquête spatiale regorge d’exemples où les éléments se sont invités lors du décollage, avec des scénarios très différents. Le cas le plus célèbre reste la mission Apollo 12, en novembre 1969. Frappée à deux reprises par la foudre pendant son ascension, la géante Saturn V avait subi une panne temporaire de ses instruments de bord et la perte de données critiques. L’équipage et le centre de contrôle avaient réussi à rétablir la situation.
D’autres n’ont pas eu cette chance. En mars 1987, une fusée américaine Atlas-Centaur frappée par un éclair a perdu son système de guidage avant de se désintégrer en pleine ascension. À l’inverse, en mai 2019, une fusée russe Soyouz avait encaissé une décharge impressionnante au décollage et poursuivi sa trajectoire comme si de rien n’était pour placer son satellite en orbite.
Un casse-tête de critères avant le feu vert
Pour se prémunir contre ces décharges destructrices, les zones de lancement sont bardées d’imposants pylônes paratonnerres et appliquent des limites météorologiques draconiennes. Avant de donner le fameux « go », les équipes de tir passent au crible une batterie de données : le champ électrique ambiant, la température et l’épaisseur des nuages, le cisaillement des vents en altitude, l’humidité ou encore l’activité solaire.
Si la mission embarque un équipage, la surveillance s’étend bien au-delà du pas de tir. Il faut aussi évaluer la visibilité et l’état de la mer dans les zones de récupération au large, afin de garantir une intervention rapide si la capsule doit s’éjecter en urgence. Un ensemble de contraintes très strictes qui explique pourquoi les reports de tir sont assez fréquents, mais absolument essentiels.

articles.title: Anthropic updates Claude voice mode with more capable models | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Weeks after OpenAI rolled out a new family of conversational models and updated ChatGPT’s voice mode, rival Anthropic is making its move to make Claude more voice-friendly with a new update. The company said Thursday that users can choose between Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models.
Claude’s voice mode, which was released last year and powered by the Haiku model, provided quick responses, but wasn’t well suited for complex work. The company said that with the new update, voice mode picks the last model people used in the text chat and uses its fastest version by default.
Anthropic said that the new voice mode can help users with longer conversations, including providing feedback on their communication style, talking through a pitch to a client, and brainstorming product market research.
What’s more, Claude’s voice mode can tap into other apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Canva, and Notion. This means that users can ask it to update a meeting slot, draft an email, or create a document in Notion.
Notably, this is a big difference from OpenAI’s voice mode, which updated its conversational style but still isn’t able to use different tools to get work done.
Earlier this year, Anthropic added multilingual support to Claude’s voice mode in beta. It said that now users can talk in various languages, but they have to manually specify the language. At the moment, Anthropic supports English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazilian), and Spanish (Latin America/Spain).
The new voice mode is available to all users in beta across platforms. However, free users will be restricted to using the Haiku model with only one connected app.
Anthropic didn’t make any changes to the voice model with this release, and it hasn’t detailed what kind of voice stack it uses. That means, unlike OpenAI’s release, users might not find any conversational improvements such as better interruption handling.

articles.title: Cambridge's TidalSense raises €16.6 million to turn the tide on respiratory diagnostics with patented AI tech | EU-Startups
articles.text:
TidalSense (formerly Cambridge Respiratory Innovations), a Cambridge-based AI-powered respiratory diagnostic, today announced a €16.6 million ($19 million) funding round to accelerate commercialisation in the UK and support globalisation of the technology, including to the USA.
The round included investment from new investor Cross-Border Impact Ventures, and returning investors BGF, Airstream Capital, and Foresight Group. This brings the company’s total funding to €35.1 million ($40 million), including €9.6 million ($11 million) grant funding from Innovate UK, SBRI, NIHR, and Asthma-Lung UK. In 2023, the company closed an €8.6 million fundraising round led by investors BGF and Downing.
Dr. Ameera Patel, CEO of TidalSense, said, “Respiratory disease has been neglected by governments and health systems for years, often overshadowed by cancer and cardiovascular disease, even though it affects one in five people. That’s finally starting to change. The World Health Organisation now recognises COPD as a global health priority, and it’s about time. Part of the problem has always been how we talk about it: COPD is widely seen as a smoker’s disease, but a quarter of cases come from air pollution and the biomass fuel millions still cook with every day.”
Founded in 2013, TidalSense builds AI-driven diagnostic and monitoring solutions for respiratory medicine built on the foundation of the company’s novel patented sensor technology, N-Tidal.
The company states that COPD is the UK’s third biggest cause of death, killing around 30,000 people a year. It further notes that it costs the NHS €2.2 billion (£1.9 billion) annually and that over half of NHS regions lack the capacity to meet current demand for spirometry testing. An estimated 1.9 million people are living with the condition, diagnosed and undiagnosed combined.
The company also highlights that at least 600k people in the UK are currently waiting for a formal COPD diagnosis. The test they are waiting for – spirometry – requires forceful exhalation, specialist training to administer, and can take nearly an hour per patient when factoring in wait and recovery time.
TidalSense claims to have built an alternative. N-Tidal Diagnose requires patients to breathe normally into a handheld device for 75 seconds, capturing a CO₂ waveform — a capnogram — of the kind traditionally used in critical care, which a set of AI models analyses to detect COPD.
The company notes that any healthcare professional can be trained to use the device in 10 minutes, with no specialist qualification required. Its AI diagnostic models have been trained on more than 2.5 million patient breaths.
TidalSense reported that, in the first post-market validation of the device, presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress in 2025 and conducted on a completely unseen patient cohort, N-Tidal Diagnose achieved over 90% performance across all key metrics of diagnostic accuracy.
“We’re still diagnosing in the 21st century with a test invented in the 1800s, and one that needs specialist equipment and training most of the world doesn’t have access to. Lower income and minority communities pay the price for that first. That’s the gap we want to close at TidalSense, and the NHS is the first place we’re doing it,” added Dr. Patel.
In March 2025, N-Tidal Diagnose software became the first non-spirometry AI diagnostic device to receive a CE mark under the EU MDR (Class IIa) for COPD. It was launched into the NHS in September 2025.
It was commissioned by Suffolk and North-East Essex Integrated Care Board, and its use has since expanded into NHS Wales, community lung screening clinics in the South of England, and now into Glasgow.
Donna Parr, Managing Partner at Cross-Border Impact Ventures, said, “We look for technology that doesn’t just have a compelling story, but a body of clinical evidence behind it. TidalSense has both, with a CEO who has lived the problem she’s solving, and a product that’s already live within the NHS healthcare environment, saving time for patients who have waited years for an answer. It is also technology that can improve access to appropriate treatment for COPD sufferers on a global basis and especially for women who are often misdiagnosed. This is exactly the kind of impact we want to make with our investments.”
TidalSense has deepened its senior bench ahead of the US expansion, with Andrew Wheeler, Director of Market Access and Public Policy, joining from NICE; Eric Mayes, Non-Executive Director, who was founding CEO of Endomagnetics; and Donna Parr, who joins the board with more than 30 years of tech and health tech investment experience.

articles.title: Gaming wird teurer: Vom Verschwinden physischer Medien und den Absichten der großen Hersteller
articles.text:
Gaming ohne physische Medien: Wieso es für Gamer teurer wird – und diese Entwicklung kein Zufall ist
Die Nachricht kam plötzlich und war trotzdem abzusehen: Per Blog-Post verkündete Playstation, kürzlich dass neue Spiele ab Januar 2028 nicht mehr auf Discs veröffentlicht werden. Es ist also davon auszugehen, dass die Playstation 6 schon ohne Disc-Laufwerk hergestellt wird. Stattdessen sollen Games nur noch über den Playstation Store und in digitaler Form im Einzelhandel erhältlich sein.
Dies sei für das Unternehmen ein „natürlicher Schritt, um sich an die Verbrauchertrends anzupassen, da die allgemeine Nachfrage nach digitalen Medien die nach physischen Datenträgern mittlerweile deutlich übersteigt“. Das ist durchaus richtig. So liegt der Anteil an digitalen Verkäufen bei Herstellern inzwischen teils bei über 90 Prozent. Dennoch dürfte dieser Schritt für viele Gamer teuer werden – und das ist kein Zufall.
Eigentlich nichts Neues – aber!
Wer auf dem PC spielt, kennt diesen Umstand schon lange. Hier ist es nichts Neues, dass Games allein in digitaler Form verkauft werden. Der Großteil davon über die Verkaufsplattform Steam. Doch es gibt einen großen Unterschied zu einem Ökosystem wie der Playstation: auf dem PC hat man die freie Wahl.
Sicherlich ist Steam die wichtigste Plattform für alle großen Entwicklerstudios. Wer mit seinem Spiel Erfolg haben will, muss hier präsent sein. Aber es gibt eben doch Alternativen. Vom Epic Games Store bis zu GOG: Gamer können auf dem PC entscheiden, wo sie ihr Spiel kaufen wollen. Und damit etwa auch Rabatte wahrnehmen, die in einem Store angeboten werden und im anderen nicht.
Wer ab 2028 sein digitales Spiel auf der Playstation kaufen möchte, hat diese Möglichkeit nicht. Die Ökosysteme der Hersteller Playstation, Xbox und Nintendo basieren darauf, dass auf ihren Konsolen nur die eigenen Verkaufsplattformen genutzt werden können. Sie allein bestimmen die Preise, Alternativen gibt es nicht.
Für die Hersteller ist das freilich sehr lukrativ. Zumal sie, anders als etwa auf dem PC, keine Abgaben an eine Plattform wie Steam zahlen müssen. Die Erlöse über den Playstation Store gehen bei den eigenen Spielen allein an Sony. Der Schritt hin zum rein Digitalen ist für das Unternehmen also ein monetär äußerst vorteilhafter.
Keine Spiele, sondern Lizenzen
Für die Gamer aber sieht es anders aus. Wo es keine Auswahl und Konkurrenz gibt, gibt es auch nur selten günstige Preise. Ein Vergleich wie auf dem PC ist nicht möglich. Zudem ermöglichen Plattformen wie GOG einen DRM-freien Kauf. Das heißt, dass Spiele ohne Kopierschutz verkauft werden, der oft eine konstante Online-Verbindung voraussetzt. Wer hier ein digitales Spiel kauft und es auf einer Festplatte speichert, kann davon ausgehen, es auch in vielen Jahren noch spielen zu können.
Auf Konsolen sieht das anders aus. Wer etwa im Playstation Store ein Spiel kauft, der erwirbt, wie auf jeder digitalen Verkaufsplattform, auch eine Lizenz – die theoretisch aber auch wieder entzogen werden kann. Doch sind diese Lizenzen hier immer an den Account gebunden. Und wenn der gesperrt wird, ist kein Zugang zum Spiel mehr möglich. Erst kürzlich machte Playstation zudem damit Schlagzeilen, dass das Unternehmen um die 500 Inhalte aus seinem Store gelöscht hat. In diesem Fall handelte es sich um Filme, die nun nicht mehr gestreamt werden können – auch wenn sie käuflich erworben wurden.
Schon seit Jahren bewegt sich die gesamte Industrie immer mehr in Richtung sogenannter Service-Games. Spiele also, die nur online gespielt werden können und darauf ausgelegt sind, dass Gamer sie über Monate, wenn nicht Jahre, spielen. Mit kontinuierlichen Updates und neuem Content. Doch wenn das Spiel nicht erfolgreich ist, werden die Server abgestellt – und das Spiel wird unbrauchbar.
In einer Zukunft ohne physische Spiele und digitalen Games, die nur noch auf hauseigenen Plattformen angeboten werden, wird dieses Risiko nochmal größer. Denn dann könnte selbst das bereits gekaufte Singleplayer-Game nicht mehr funktionieren, wenn es aus dem digitalen Geschäft verschwindet oder der eigene Account nicht mehr aktiv ist. Und auch das kann für die Hersteller lukrativ sein. Ältere Services, die kein oder nur noch wenig Geld bringen, gleichzeitig aber Kosten für Server oder Updates aufwerfen, werden einfach abgestellt.
Codes in Plastikhüllen
Im Blogpost erwähnt Playstation noch die Möglichkeit, dass Spiele auch 2028 noch im Einzelhandel angeboten werden können: „in digitalen Formaten“. Wahrscheinlich sind damit Codes in Spieleverpackungen gemeint, so wie es bei Grand Theft Auto 6 bereits der Fall ist. Doch es ist davon auszugehen, dass das nur eine Übergangslösung ist. Die wenigsten Gamer dürften Interesse daran haben, sich Verpackungen zu kaufen, die nur einen Code enthalten.
Denn anders als etwa bei den Game Key Cards von Nintendo, für die es auch einige Kritik gab, können diese Codes nur einmalig verwendet werden. Einmal eingelöst, ist das Spiel dann an den jeweiligen Account gebunden. Ein Wiederverkauf ist nicht möglich. Und damit ist das wichtigste Argument für den Kauf physischer Medien hinfällig.
Mit diesem Schritt von Playstation dürfte zudem die Wahrscheinlichkeit steigen, dass eine Playstation 6 kein Disc-Laufwerk mehr verbaut haben wird. Sollte es so kommen, könnten somit auch keine älteren Playstation-Spiele, die noch auf Disc gekauft wurden, auf der neuen Konsole abgespielt werden. Auch sie werden somit wertlos.
Nach wie vor sind gebrauchte Spiele für viele Gamer die einzige Möglichkeit, sich überhaupt ein Spiel leisten zu können. Auch mit dem Wissen, dass sie ihr Spiel schließlich selbst wieder werden verkaufen können. Digitale Spiele, ob nun über den Playstation Store oder als Code in einer Plastikverpackung, verschließen auch diesen Zugang zum Gaming. Die Zukunft für Gamer dürfte also nicht nur in Bezug auf Hardware teuer werden.

articles.title: Cómo saber qué barra de sonido es la ideal para tu televisor y hogar
articles.text:
Frente a la limitación de los parlantes integrados en la mayoría de los televisores modernos, surge la necesidad de buscar alternativas que eleven la experiencia audiovisual y las barras de sonido suelen ser una de las primeras opciones por su facilidad de uso.
Sin embargo, elegir un dispositivo adecuado a las necesidades y las dimensiones del hogar es fundamental, para que el sonido se distribuya de la mejor manera posible, entregando la experiencia que estamos buscando.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué es una barra de sonido y cómo funciona
Una barra de sonido es un dispositivo compacto y alargado, diseñado para mejorar la calidad de audio de un televisor. Su función principal es ofrecer un sonido más claro, potente y envolvente que el que proporcionan los altavoces de fábrica.
Estas barras integran varios altavoces en su interior, como tweeters para las frecuencias agudas, altavoces medios para los diálogos y woofers para los graves. Al combinarse, logran crear un espacio sonoro más amplio y realista, capaz de resaltar tanto los diálogos como los efectos especiales de cualquier contenido.
PUBLICIDAD
Algunos modelos avanzados incorporan tecnologías como Dolby Atmos, que proyecta el sonido hacia el techo y las paredes para simular una experiencia tridimensional.
La instalación de una barra de sonido suele ser sencilla: basta con conectarla mediante HDMI ARC, óptico digital o incluso Bluetooth, según las opciones del televisor y la barra.
PUBLICIDAD
Tipos de barra de sonido según canales y tecnología
La cantidad de canales determina la complejidad y capacidad envolvente de una barra de sonido, según informes de marcas como Sonos y JBL. Las opciones más comunes son:
- 2.0: Dos altavoces (izquierda y derecha), que mejoran el estéreo básico.
- 2.1: Añaden un subwoofer para graves más potentes.
- 3.0 o 3.1: Incluyen un canal central que refuerza los diálogos, con o sin subwoofer.
- 5.1: Incorporan canales traseros y subwoofer, simulando el sonido envolvente clásico.
- 5.1.2 o 7.1.4: Modelos compatibles con Dolby Atmos, que agregan altavoces orientados al techo para un efecto tridimensional.
La elección del número de canales depende del tamaño de la sala y del tipo de contenido que más se consume. Para una experiencia cinematográfica inmersiva, los modelos con Dolby Atmos y canales de altura ofrecen una ventaja clara, mientras que para el uso diario en habitaciones pequeñas, una barra 2.1 puede ser suficiente.
PUBLICIDAD
Factores clave para elegir la barra de sonido adecuada
- Espacio disponible: la barra debe guardar proporción con el tamaño del televisor y el ambiente. En habitaciones pequeñas, modelos compactos optimizan el espacio, mientras que en salas amplias conviene invertir en barras más grandes y potentes.
- Compatibilidad y conectividad: verifica que la barra cuente con las entradas necesarias (HDMI ARC/eARC, óptico, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi). Los televisores más recientes suelen ser compatibles con HDMI eARC, que permite el máximo rendimiento de las tecnologías de sonido envolvente.
- Tipo de uso: quienes priorizan películas y series pueden preferir modelos con Dolby Atmos y subwoofer dedicado. Para videojuegos, es relevante la baja latencia y la posibilidad de conectar la consola directamente a la barra. En el caso de los aficionados a la música, conviene priorizar la calidad del procesamiento estéreo y las opciones de conectividad inalámbrica.
Consejos prácticos y errores comunes al elegir una barra de sonido
Un error frecuente es comprar una barra sin verificar la compatibilidad de entradas con el televisor, lo que puede limitar su uso o requerir adaptadores. Otro fallo habitual consiste en pensar que una barra económica ofrecerá siempre un sonido envolvente real, cuando en realidad la tecnología y la cantidad de canales son determinantes para este tipo de experiencia.
Empresas como Samsung advierten que la potencia, medida en watts, no es el único parámetro importante: la calidad del sonido y su adaptación al espacio son factores clave. Para habitaciones grandes, conviene priorizar modelos con subwoofer y, si es posible, parlantes traseros, mientras que en espacios pequeños basta con una barra compacta y eficiente.
PUBLICIDAD
La barra de sonido ideal es aquella que responde al uso cotidiano del hogar, se integra armónicamente con el televisor y el espacio, y satisface las expectativas de calidad de audio en función del presupuesto disponible.
Medir el espacio, revisar las especificaciones del televisor y tener claras las necesidades de uso son los pasos esenciales para elegir correctamente y transformar la experiencia frente a la pantalla.

articles.title: Alexa Plus is getting an AI update to handle more complicated instructions
articles.text:
Amazon is launching an update to its Alexa Plus assistant that will allow it to connect to smart home devices in new ways. With the update, which is currently in preview, Alexa Plus can link up with tech from Bosch, Delta, Ecovacs, iRobot, Yale Home, Whirlpool, Tapo, Eufy, and others, while automatically routing requests to the correct device.
Alexa Plus is getting an AI update to handle more complicated instructions
Amazon’s upgraded AI assistant will be able to do more across a wider range of smart home devices.
Amazon’s upgraded AI assistant will be able to do more across a wider range of smart home devices.
In an example shared by Amazon, a person with a supported washing machine can say, “Alexa, my kid’s soccer jersey could use a deep clean, but the tag says cold wash only.” From there, Alexa Plus would navigate the washer’s cycle options and choose the correct setting. The new integrations are powered by Amazon’s new AI developer toolkit, which is supposed to make it easier for device makers to connect to Alexa Plus, “including those with unique capabilities that weren’t supported before.”
Amazon widely launched its revamped AI assistant in February, which can handle multi-step requests and help you create routines using your voice. It currently only performs tasks in a limited number of third-party services, such as Ticketmaster, OpenTable, Uber, Thumbtack, Expedia, Yelp, Square, and Angi.
But Amazon is trying to change this by adopting the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open-source standard that allows AI models to connect to external systems and tools. This will give more brands the ability to interact with Alexa Plus, with Canva, Headspace, Priceline, Lyft, Cengage, Virgin Atlantic, Weekend, and other companies launching integrations later this year.
For example, Priceline will give customers the ability to browse hotel options and book a trip directly through Alexa Plus. Priceline, along with Atom Tickets, Cengage, Fandango, and Taskrabbit, will soon support payments through Amazon Wallet as well.

articles.title: White House report says Trump can usher in a "new golden age" of science
articles.text:
On Tuesday, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) released a report entitled “Science: A New Golden Age,” in which it lays out how it has viewed science, found it lacking, and believes the Trump administration is in the perfect position to fix things. It’s a bit unexpected coming from an administration that has been proposing crippling funding cuts to research and trying to enable political appointees to terminate grants awarded based on scientific merit.
The report presents itself as the spiritual successor of “Science, the Endless Frontier,” a policy document that laid out the case for government-funded science in the wake of World War II. The New Golden Age (SNGA) says that, while the concepts promoted by the original remain vital, the circumstances have changed such that we need major revisions to how the government is implementing things.
The result is an odd mix. It completely ignores or glosses over many things that the administration is doing to harm scientific progress. In some cases, it identifies issues that have already been discussed as problems within the scientific community. Elsewhere, it’s a mixture of political grievances, ideas without a solid intellectual foundation, and an injection of Silicon Valley’s perspective on innovation (Michael Kratsios, the director of the OSTP, formerly worked with Peter Thiel). As a result, it’s unlikely to have anything like the impact of “Science, the Endless Frontier.”
Lacking internal coherence
The report is trying to make the case that US government-funded science has some structural problems, serious enough that they require major changes to the entire enterprise. (It also makes a positive argument, namely that developments in AI necessitate a new approach, which we’ll come back to.) Some of those concerns are real and had been discussed within the research community previously.
One of the real problems it discusses is the amount of time researchers need to spend on writing grants and performing administrative tasks, taking away from their time doing research. SNGA promises to relieve this by simplifying regulations and streamlining the grant application process. But it’s also remarkably vague, in that its authors do not identify a single regulation that is in need of reform.

articles.title: Applications open for latest Harambeans cohort - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Applications open for the latest cohort of the Harambeans, African innovators who pledge “to work together as one” to unlock the potential of Africa.
Founded in 2008, the Harambeans describe themselves as an “alliance of determined entrepreneurs who are building Africa’s future” and “visionaries transforming Africa’s challenges into opportunities”.
Over the last decade, Harambeans has spawned a series of tech-enabled ventures such as Andela, Flutterwave, and Yoco, which have collectively generated over 3,000 jobs, raised over US$1 billion from Google Ventures, CRE Ventures and Accel.
It receives over 3,000 applications per year, and has 30 spots in each class. Applications are open here until October 31.

articles.title: Le dernier vélo électrique urbain d’Intersport perd déjà 300 €
articles.text:
À première vue, le Crosslite de Nakamura a des airs de vélo sportif. Ce VAE d’Intersport est pourtant bien un vélo de ville, mais qui mélange deux genres pour plus de polyvalence. Si vous recherchez un deux-roues léger et pratique au quotidien pour vous rendre au travail ou circuler en ville, mais également emprunter de temps à autre quelques chemins moins balisés, Intersport tient le bon modèle, en ce moment en promotion.
Le vélo de ville électrique Nakamura Crosslite est commercialisé à 1 899,99 € depuis sa sortie en mars 2026. Il est en ce moment remisé au prix de 1 599,99 € sur le site d’Intersport.
C’est quoi, ce VAE de ville Nakamura ?
Le Crosslite mise sur une conception plutôt légère et minimaliste, avec un cadre en aluminium associé à une fourche en carbone. Du style, il en a, avec ses belles lignes élancées. Avec un poids d’environ 20 kg, le vélo électrique de Nakamura offre une conduite souple en ville. Couplé à une bonne ergonomie globale, Intersport propose ici un vélo agréable à piloter en toutes circonstances. Il faut toutefois aimer la conduite sportive qu’apporte sa position active.
Le Nakamura Crosslite embarque un moteur électrique de 250 W installé dans le moyeu arrière, capable de délivrer jusqu’à 42 Nm de couple. Le vélo dispose également d’un capteur de couple, censé offrir une assistance plus naturelle et réactive dès les premiers coups de pédale. Dans les faits, l’assistance est effectivement correctement délivrée pour une aide efficace. La transmission monovitesse par courroie est dotée d’un capteur de couple qui permet de démarrer sans effort.
À ce prix, le Nakamura Crosslite est-il une bonne affaire ?
300 € de réduction pour un VAE sorti en mars dernier, c’est une très bonne affaire, surtout que le Nakamura Crosslite est un deux-roues de qualité. Le vélo embarque une béquille, des éclairages avant et arrière, et un garde-boue, ainsi qu’une fonction de verrouillage Bluetooth afin de sécuriser le vélo. Malheureusement, il faudra se passer de connectivité avec l’appli Nakamura.
Côté autonomie, le vélo embarque une batterie intégrée de 345 Wh, qui permet de parcourir jusqu’à 70 km dans des conditions optimales selon Nakamura. Son chargeur rapide permettrait de récupérer 80 % de la batterie en environ deux heures, pour une recharge complète en moins de trois heures. Une batterie additionnelle de 250 Wh peut également être ajoutée séparément pour augmenter la capacité.

articles.title: Ce monstre chinois de l'e-commerce veut conquérir l’Europe, Bruxelles lui barre la route
articles.text:
JD.com, le géant chinois de l’e-commerce, veut mettre un pied solide en Europe en rachetant Ceconomy. Mais la Commission européenne soupçonne l’entreprise d’avoir été dopée par des subventions chinoises pour emporter la mise, et elle exige des comptes.
Fondé à Pékin en 1998 par Richard Liu, JD.com n’est autre que le numéro 2 de l’e-commerce chinois, juste derrière Alibaba. Sa force ? Une logistique intégrée hors norme, avec plus de 1 600 entrepôts et 200 000 livreurs, qui lui permet de livrer plus de 90 % de ses commandes en moins de 24 heures. De quoi peser aujourd’hui plus de 180 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires par an.
En Europe, le groupe reste pourtant un nouveau venu. Après l’échec de sa plateforme Ochama, JD.com a lancé en mars dernier Joybuy, un site de vente en ligne accessible en France, en Allemagne, au Royaume-Uni et au Benelux. Une arrivée discrète, mais qui s’inscrit dans une ambition bien plus large : s’imposer physiquement sur le marché européen.
Rachat d’un géant européen
Et pour cela, l’entreprise tente de racheter Ceconomy, le géant allemand de l’électronique grand public, propriétaire des enseignes MediaMarkt et Saturn. Celles-ci comptent des centaines de magasins physiques répartis dans plusieurs pays du Vieux Continent, en plus d’une activité de vente en ligne bien installée. Le groupe possède, en outre, une participation minoritaire dans Fnac Darty.
L’englober permettrait à JD.com de réaliser un raccourci en or : au lieu de construire patiemment sa présence en Europe magasin par magasin, la société chinoise récupérerait d’un coup un réseau physique déjà solide, une clientèle fidèle et une marque qui inspire confiance. De quoi transformer son arrivée discrète avec Joybuy en une implantation bien plus musclée, appuyée sur sa force logistique et technologique.
Ainsi, l’opération, chiffrée à 2,5 milliards de dollars, a été officiellement notifiée à la Commission européenne le 17 avril dernier. Mais visiblement, les régulateurs, déjà sceptiques face à Shein, AliExpress ou Temu, ne sont pas convaincus.
Un possible financement chinois
Depuis le mois de mai, la Commission mène une enquête approfondie sur cette acquisition au titre du règlement sur les subventions étrangères, un texte entré en vigueur en 2023 pour éviter qu’une entreprise ne fausse la concurrence en Europe grâce à des aides publiques venues d’un pays tiers.
Concrètement, Bruxelles soupçonne le groupe d’avoir bénéficié de financements préférentiels, d’avantages fiscaux et de subventions accordés par Pékin. De quoi lui permettre, potentiellement, de surenchérir sur Ceconomy et de proposer des conditions qu’un concurrent européen n’aurait pas pu égaler. La Commission veut aussi vérifier qu’une fois la fusion actée, l’entité combinée ne profitera pas de cet argent public pour prendre un avantage déloyal sur le marché européen de l’électronique.
De son côté, JD.com reste confiante et s'attend à une issue positive d’ici à la fin de l’année, révèle Reuters. La Commission, elle, a jusqu’au 2 octobre pour trancher : elle peut accepter des engagements de la part du groupe chinois, interdire purement l’opération, ou donner son feu vert sans condition.

articles.title: Hackers abuse Notepad++ plugins to stealthily install malware
articles.text:
Ukraine's CERT has uncovered attacks distributing an archive containing the legitimate Notepad++ application and a malicious utility called LunchPoke disguised as a plugin to establish persistence.
The campaign has been attributed to a threat cluster tracked as UAC-0099, which primarily targets organizations in Ukraine and has previously been linked to providing initial access for attacks carried out by APT44, also known as Sandworm.
The attackers do not exploit any vulnerability or a supply-chain compromise impacting the popular software.
Notepad++ attack chain
CERT-UA observed that UAC-0099 changed their modus operandi recently and now delivers a ZIP archive with a VBS script disguised as a PDF document. When launched, the PDF retrieves another compressed file named Evernote.zip.
The second archive contains a complete copy of the legitimate editor Notepad++ version 8.8.3, a malicious plugin (NppExport.dll), a password-protected archive (updater.rar), and the legitimate WinRAR executable.
The VBS script installs the package into a randomly named directory, launches Notepad++, and then loads the malicious NppExport.dll via the application’s normal plugin-loading mechanism.
CERT-UA explains that this DLL is LunchPoke, a tool that creates a scheduled task on Windows and extracts the contents of the RAR file, including RemoteLibUpdater.exe and InitTest.dll.
The executable in the RAR file is BurnyBear, a loader for the DLL file that is the MatchBoil V2 malware loader.
BurnyBear also features a fallback mechanism in case launching RemoteLibUpdater.exe fails, triggering a resource exhaustion attack targeting the host’s RAM and CPU.
The latter creates another scheduled task, updates its configuration and command-and-control (C2) address, and then uses WinRAR to extract downloaded programs.
CERT-UA does not mention the final payloads delivered in the observed attacks, the purpose of the campaign, or the targeted organizations.
The researchers mention CVE-2025-56383, a DLL hijacking flaw in Notepad++ v8.8.3, the exact version used in these attacks, but note that the Notepad++ team has disputed this issue, claiming that plugin loading is standard functionality.
CERT-UA advises system administrators to update Notepad++ to version 8.9.7, 7-Zip to version 26.02, and WinRAR to version 7.23, to prevent hackers from exploiting known flaws in existing products and enabling stealthy attacks.

articles.title: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, July 23, 2026.
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 23, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, July 23, 2026.
Community agriculture is the way forward for farmers to enhance their livelihoods even as Indian startups continue to raise funding, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
This woman entrepreneur is helping small farmers earn more through community-supported agriculture
Spudnik Farms, founded by Sumeet Kaur, connects urban consumers with local farmers through a subscription model. The company works with 250 farmers across Karnataka, helping them earn higher incomes while promoting seasonal, indigenous and sustainably grown produce.
Funding news
Banking tech company BusinessNext raises $40M from ServiceNow
Workplace management software company ServiceNow has announced an investment of $40 million in BusinessNext, a Noida-headquartered technology firm focused on banking and financial services industry. The Series C round has valued BusinessNext at $700 million and is aimed at strengthening the company's efforts to drive autonomous operations and private AI solutions across banking and financial services.
Tech30 startup CARPL.ai raises $10M in Series A led by IFC
CARPL.ai, a radiology AI marketplace and enterprise platform, has raised $10 million in a Series A round of funding led by International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private sector arm of the World Bank Group, with participation from Stellaris Venture Partners and other investors. CARPL.ai was part of the YourStory Tech30 cohort of 2022.
Farm Watt Innovations raises Rs 32.5 Cr to expand bioenergy network
Farm Watt Innovations has raised Rs 32.5 crore in a funding round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter to strengthen India's bioenergy supply chain. The climate-focused agribusiness converts agricultural waste into biomass for compressed biogas (CBG) plants and other renewable energy applications, helping reduce stubble burning and greenhouse gas emissions while creating rural livelihoods.
The fresh capital will be used to expand biomass collection networks, establish additional aggregation hubs, invest in machinery and strengthen its workforce. Going forward, the company plans to develop its own portfolio of CBG, bio-pellet and biochar plants, creating an integrated circular bioeconomy platform that delivers environmental, social and economic benefits.
Wiffy secures $3 million Series A funding
Home improvement services platform Wiffy has raised $3 million in a Series A funding round led by Earth Fund, with participation from Persol Holdings of Japan and existing investor Capria Ventures. The company provides post-sales installation and maintenance services for more than 100 brands, including IKEA, Panasonic, Godrej, Hettich and Amazon.
The proceeds will be used to enhance its technology platform, strengthen AI-powered workforce management, expand enterprise partnerships and enter new service categories. Wiffy operates through a network of over 5,000 certified technicians and has served more than one million homes across 100 cities, while maintaining a business model driven primarily by enterprise partnerships.
NeuralKart raises Rs 2.35 Cr in seed funding
AI-powered insurtech startup NeuralKart has raised Rs 2.35 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The Bengaluru-based company develops AI-driven decision-making tools that automate insurance underwriting, claims processing and industrial safety assessments. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen product development, expand AI and machine learning capabilities, and accelerate customer acquisition and go-to-market initiatives.
NeuralKart said it has already secured paying enterprise customers and maintains a 100% customer retention rate. The company works with leading insurers and industrial risk services firms and has also entered into a co-development partnership for its FieldSense platform, targeting the growing insurance automation and industrial safety technology markets.
Upkraft secures Rs 1.6 Cr in pre-seed round
AI-powered extracurricular learning platform Upkraft has raised Rs 1.6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from angel investors, entrepreneurs and early-stage ecosystem players. Founded by Tejasvi Singh Kushwah, Varun Mangal and Kritika Varandani, the startup offers structured extracurricular learning programmes for students at homes, schools and residential communities.
The company will use the proceeds to develop AI-powered personalised learning tools, expand operations across Bengaluru and Gurugram, strengthen its technology platform and build teams across product, engineering, sales and tutor operations. Over the next 12 to 18 months, Upkraft aims to increase student enrolments and deepen its presence in key markets.
Other news
Utho Cloud to deploy 10,000 GPUs for sovereign AI
Utho Cloud has announced plans to deploy 10,000 GPUs over the next seven to eight quarters to strengthen India's sovereign AI infrastructure. The investment will include NVIDIA's H200, H100, A100, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and L4 GPUs, enabling enterprises, startups, researchers and government organisations to access high-performance AI computing hosted entirely within India.
The company said its platform will offer predictable pricing in Indian rupees, guaranteed GPU availability, data residency compliant with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and 24x7 support. With more than 51,000 users, Utho aims to reduce dependence on overseas cloud infrastructure while providing secure AI computing capabilities for domestic organisations.
Google concludes Build with AI parliamentary showcase
Google has concluded the Parliamentary Showcase of its Build with AI: Code for Communities programme, an initiative aimed at connecting AI innovation with public governance. Organised with The Dialogue, the programme saw 12 winning developer teams present AI-powered solutions before Members of Parliament.
More than 7,000 developers from over 18 Indian cities participated, creating over 1,000 open-source projects using Google's Gemini and Gemma AI models. The solutions addressed civic governance, public health, agriculture and environmental challenges. Google said selected projects will now be piloted in parliamentary constituencies, demonstrating how AI can be used to improve public service delivery and community welfare across the country.
Cars24 Labs partners Startup Policy Forum on AI
Cars24 Labs, the AI innovation arm of Cars24, has partnered with the Startup Policy Forum (SPF) to support responsible AI adoption and policy development in India. Under the partnership, Cars24 Labs will contribute to AI policy discussions, founder engagements, industry dialogues and global immersion programmes while sharing practical insights from deploying AI across its business. SPF represents more than 75 new-age companies and works to strengthen India's startup ecosystem. The collaboration aims to bring together founders, policymakers, researchers and technology leaders to exchange ideas and help shape AI policy. Cars24 Labs said the initiative reflects its commitment to supporting India's emergence as a global leader in artificial intelligence.
Cashfree Payments waives gateway fees for new merchants
Cashfree Payments has introduced a limited-period offer waiving payment gateway charges for new businesses on the first Rs 20 lakh of gross merchandise value (GMV) processed through its platform until March 31, 2027. The initiative is aimed at helping small and growing businesses improve cash flow ahead of the festive season. Besides the fee waiver, new merchants will benefit from onboarding within minutes, next-day settlements and dedicated account managers during the peak sales period. Cashfree said the move will allow businesses to reinvest savings into inventory, marketing and logistics while simplifying digital payments and reducing operational costs for small and medium enterprises.
Wipro Consumer Care acquires Good Home and Eva brands
Wipro Consumer Care & Lighting has signed definitive agreements to acquire the Good Home and Eva brands from TTK Healthcare Ltd. for Rs 256 crore. The acquisition strengthens Wipro's presence in the home care and personal care segments. Good Home offers products including air fresheners, scrubbers and drain cleaners, while Eva is among India's established deodorant brands with body sprays, perfumes, roll-ons and talcum powders. Together, the two brands generated Rs 148 crore in revenue during FY26. Wipro said the acquisition aligns with its strategy of expanding into trusted, high-growth consumer categories driven by rising hygiene awareness, premiumisation and evolving lifestyle preferences.
Campus Fund appoints Howard Morgan to advisory board
Campus Fund, a venture capital firm focused on student- and dropout-led startups, has appointed veteran investor Dr. Howard L. Morgan to its Global Advisory Board. Morgan is Chair and General Partner at B Capital and co-founder of First Round Capital, an early investor in companies including Uber, Square, Roblox and Notion. His appointment comes as Campus Fund deploys its third and largest fund— a $100 million corpus announced in June 2025 — to support up to 60 startups over four years. The fund evaluates more than 7,000 startups annually through a network of over 100 student scouts, with investments spanning deeptech, space technology and climate technology.
Quest Global named leader in ISG semiconductor study
Engineering services firm Quest Global has been recognised as a Leader in the ISG Provider Lens Semiconductor Industry Services and Solutions 2026 Study for the US market. The company earned leadership positions in Design, Test and Verification Services and Manufacturing and Engineering Services. ISG highlighted Quest Global's capabilities across silicon engineering, custom SoC and ASIC development, embedded systems and manufacturing engineering. The report also recognised the company's "Silicon to Systems to Cloud" approach and AI-enabled engineering methodologies, which help semiconductor companies reduce design cycles, improve first-pass silicon success and accelerate the development of next-generation semiconductor products.
InCred Asset Management crosses Rs 1,000 crore healthcare AUM
InCred Asset Management has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in investments across listed healthcare companies through its portfolio management services, becoming one of India's largest dedicated healthcare PMS providers. Launched in February 2021, the healthcare strategy has delivered a 18.97% CAGR, outperforming the BSE 500 TRI's 13.27% CAGR, according to the company. The portfolios invest across pharmaceuticals, hospitals, diagnostics, medical technology and contract research businesses. InCred said the milestone reflects growing investor confidence in India's healthcare sector, supported by structural factors such as rising healthcare spending, expanding insurance coverage, favourable demographics and increasing innovation in healthcare services.
Konnect Insights launches AI-powered Research Cloud
Customer experience platform Konnect Insights has launched Konnect Research Cloud (KRC), an AI-powered intelligence platform designed to help enterprises analyse customer data across multiple systems using natural language queries. The platform connects with existing customer-facing technology stacks and delivers evidence-backed insights in seconds to support business decision-making. KRC marks the first step towards the company's vision of building a Front Office Operating System that unifies enterprise technologies through AI. The solution is immediately available to enterprise customers worldwide. Konnect Insights operates cloud infrastructure across India, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the US, the UK and Germany to ensure compliance with regional data residency requirements.
PhysicsWallah partners NWWA to support Navy families
Education company PhysicsWallah (PW) has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Indian Navy Welfare & Wellness Association (NWWA) to provide educational support to the families of Indian Navy personnel. Under the initiative, families of Navy martyrs and personnel who died during service will receive full scholarships, while serving and retired personnel's families will be eligible for discounts on PW's offline coaching and online courses. The scholarships cover preparation for competitive examinations including JEE, NEET, UPSC, SSC CGL and state public service commissions. Applications will be jointly verified by NWWA and PW, with the programme aimed at making quality education more accessible to defence families across India.
FincFriends reports 43% growth in assets under management
Digital lending NBFC FincFriends reported a 43% year-on-year increase in assets under management to Rs 875 crore in FY26, while revenue rose 33% to Rs 999 crore. Loan disbursements during the year climbed to Rs 3,732 crore, compared with Rs 2,585 crore in the previous fiscal. The company said it has served more than 5.5 million borrowers since inception and currently processes around 3,000 digital loans every day. Looking ahead, FincFriends plans to expand its customer base, strengthen partnerships, improve portfolio quality and grow its near-prime lending business through higher-ticket loans, supported by a profitable business model and strong institutional backing.
Workday launches AI-powered learning platform with Sana
Workday has announced the general availability of Workday Learning, powered by Sana, an AI-driven learning solution designed to deliver personalised employee training. The platform combines Workday's workforce and skills data with Sana's AI capabilities to provide tailored learning recommendations, AI tutoring and automated course creation. Administrators can also use AI to streamline assignments and learning campaigns, reducing manual effort. The integrated solution is now available globally for Workday Human Capital Management customers, while Sana Learn will also be offered as a standalone product for organisations not using Workday's HR or financial management platforms.
StraitsMicro unveils sovereign surveillance chip family
Singapore-based StraitsMicro has unveiled Visora, a sovereign camera System-on-Chip (SoC) family designed as an indigenous alternative for surveillance systems following India's restrictions on Chinese surveillance chips. The new semiconductor platform is aimed at government, defence, smart city and critical infrastructure applications in India and overseas. Developed with Bengaluru-based design partner Proxelera and distributor Aqtronics, Visora features AI acceleration, low-power multicore processors, advanced video compression and edge AI capabilities including facial recognition, crowd analytics and behavioural analysis. The company said the platform supports India's drive towards secure, locally developed semiconductor technologies for surveillance infrastructure.
Bijliride expands student EV rental programme
Electric mobility platform Bijliride has expanded its Project Udaan initiative by launching a student-focused electric two-wheeler rental programme across major Indian cities. The scheme offers flexible, zero-commitment EV rentals while integrating optional micro-gig delivery opportunities that allow students to offset their daily rental costs. The company said the initiative addresses commuting challenges and promotes financial independence without requiring long working hours. Bijliride has reported steady growth in registrations across Hyderabad, Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi-NCR, with students using the vehicles for internships, examinations and skill development programmes. The company believes the initiative will encourage sustainable mobility and increase electric vehicle adoption among young consumers.
Enmovil appoints Jayaraman Krishnamurthy as global sales head
AI-native supply chain orchestration platform Enmovil Solutions has appointed Jayaraman Krishnamurthy as its Head of Global Sales to drive international expansion across India, the US and the Asia-Pacific region. Krishnamurthy brings over 25 years of experience in enterprise software, manufacturing and supply chain, having held leadership roles at Asian Paints, SAP, Capillary Technologies and o9 Solutions. In his new role, he will lead the company's global sales strategy and strengthen its presence in key international markets. Enmovil said the appointment comes as manufacturers increasingly adopt digital supply chain solutions, positioning the company to capitalise on growing global demand for AI-driven supply chain intelligence platforms.
ePlane, Apollo Hospitals partner on electric air ambulances
The ePlane Company and Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd. have signed a memorandum of understanding to introduce electric air ambulances and medical delivery drones into India's emergency healthcare network. Under the partnership, ePlane's e200X aircraft will be deployed for rapid inter-hospital patient transfers, trauma care, cardiac emergencies and organ transport, while its subsidiary Amber Wings will provide drones for transporting blood, medicines, vaccines and diagnostic samples.
Apollo will explore potential orders for the aircraft and drones and may consider a strategic investment in ePlane. The companies will also work with aviation regulators to develop the infrastructure needed for advanced air mobility in healthcare.
Vertiv names Raghavendra Kale India channel leader
Critical digital infrastructure provider Vertiv has promoted Raghavendra Kale as its Channel Leader for India. In his new role, Kale will lead the company's channel sales strategy, expand its partner ecosystem and strengthen engagement across key reseller and distribution segments. He previously served as Director, West Zone, Channel, where he played a key role in improving operations and driving business growth. With nearly three decades of industry experience, Kale is expected to help scale Vertiv's partner-led business strategy while nurturing strategic accounts and expanding the company's market reach in India amid growing demand for digital infrastructure solutions.
BULLET appoints Apurba Sen as VP, Business Strategy & Sales
Microdrama platform BULLET, backed by ZEE Entertainment Enterprises, has appointed Apurba Sen as Vice President, Business Strategy & Sales. The appointment comes after the launch of Trinetra AI, the company's AI-powered filmmaking and content intelligence platform.
Sen will oversee strategic initiatives across BULLET Microdrama, Trinetra AI and future business ventures, focusing on partnerships, fundraising, commercial expansion and international growth. He brings more than two decades of experience in advertising technology, streaming, connected TV, AI-driven creative technologies and digital platforms. The company said the appointment strengthens its leadership team as it expands its AI-enabled entertainment ecosystem.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft va enfin moderniser les éléments hérités de Windows 95
articles.text:
Vous ne pourrez bientôt plus vous moquer de Microsoft et de son habitude de réutiliser des éléments d’interface d’anciennes versions de Windows dans Windows 11. La firme de Redmond est en effet en train de plancher sur la modernisation de certains éléments d’interface datant de l’époque de Windows 95, toujours utilisés sur Windows 11.
Le système d’exploitation de Microsoft s’appuie en effet toujours sur une grande partie de code hérité des précédentes versions de Windows, ce qui a valu à Microsoft de nombreuses moqueries, comme avec cet utilisateur de Twitter / X qui dévoilait, avec beaucoup d’ironie, son admiration de pouvoir « parcourir 25 ans d’histoire du design d’interface en cliquant 3 fois sur Windows 11 ».
it's beautiful that I can traverse through 25 years of UI design history by clicking 3 times on Windows 11. pic.twitter.com/PyOtnoDE3j
— Elvin (@elvin_not_11) March 24, 2026
Parmi les éléments les plus fréquemment évoqués, la boite de dialogue Propriétés, ou encore la fenêtre Exécuter, reviennent souvent. Bonne nouvelle, ces éléments vont profiter d’un gros coup de pinceau de la part de Microsoft.
La boîte de dialogue des Propriétés d’un fichier enfin modernisée
Comme souvent, c’est le leaker Phantomofearth, habitué à décortiquer les builds de Windows 11, qui a repéré les changements à venir pour la fenêtre des Propriétés des fichiers.
Windows 11’s File Properties sheets are finally getting some WinUI + dark mode love! A modern version of the Properties UI is hidden in Experimental build 26300.8935, currently only for the deleted files dialog with more to come. So nice to see after all these years! 🥳
— phantomofearth 🌳 (@phantomofearth.bsky.social) 21 juillet 2026 à 22:48
« Les pages de propriétés des fichiers de Windows 11 bénéficient enfin d’une cure de jouvence WinUI et du mode sombre ! Une version moderne de l’interface des propriétés est dissimulée dans la build expérimentale 26300.8935 ; elle ne concerne pour l’instant que la boîte de dialogue de suppression des fichiers, mais d’autres éléments suivront. Quel plaisir de voir cela après toutes ces années ! 🥳 » s’est-il réjoui sur Bluesky.
En effet, Microsoft a entrepris de remplacer l’actuelle fenêtre de Propriétés de l’Explorateur de fichiers qui s’ouvre lorsque vous voulez plus de détails sur un fichier, par une version modernisée. Pour y arriver, la firme de Redmond abandonne donc la base technique héritée de Windows 95 et s’appuie sur le framework natif WinUI 3.
Grâce cette nouvelle base technique, cette fenêtre pourra enfin s’afficher en prenant en charge le thème sombre de Windows 11 lorsqu’il est utilisé. Plus globalement, cette nouvelle interface, modernisée, reprend les codes graphiques actuels utilisés pour une meilleure cohérence avec le reste de Windows 11. On y retrouvera ainsi des coins arrondis pour les cases à cocher ou encore des indicateurs d’accentuation.
Une modernisation nécessaire, mais complexe
En modernisant ces éléments d’interface hérités d’anciennes versions de Windows, Microsoft fait face à certains problèmes. La firme de Redmond doit en effet s’assurer de ne pas casser les logiciels existants, dont certains sont eux aussi anciens, et qui utilisent ces éléments d’interface hérités de Windows. C’est le cas, par exemple, avec des applications comme 7-zip ou encore Dropbox qui ajoutent leurs propres onglets dans la fenêtre Propriétés des fichiers via une interface spécifique.
Pour éviter de casser ces intégrations, Microsoft doit donc encapsuler les anciennes fenêtres de dialogue à l’intérieur de la structure moderne développée en WinUI.
 L’autre point sur lequel Microsoft doit faire preuve de vigilance concerne les performances. Les interfaces WinUI ont souvent été critiquées pour leur lenteur par rapport aux anciennes interfaces Win32. La firme de Redmond travaille donc à optimiser WinUI 3 pour s’éviter des problèmes et s’assurer que les nouveaux menus seront au moins aussi réactifs que les anciens.
La fenêtre Propriétés ne sera a priori pas la seule à bénéficier d’une modernisation. Microsoft planche également depuis plusieurs mois sur la fenêtre Exécuter dont l’interface n’a pas bougé d’un iota depuis Windows 7. La nouvelle mouture sera ainsi plus rapide, et intégrera de nouvelles fonctionnalités, comme la possibilité d’utiliser des raccourcis comme « ~\ » pour accéder directement au répertoire utilisateur.

articles.title: Clayface : le film d'horreur de DC s'offre une bande-annonce malaisante à souhait
articles.text:
Clayface : le film d'horreur de DC s'offre une bande-annonce malaisante à souhait
Clayface (ou Gueule d'Argile en VF), grand méchant de l'univers Batman, a droit à son propre film attendu en octobre dans les salles obscures. Découvrez sa bande-annonce.
DC Studios a levé le voile sur le trailer officiel du film Clayface, dont la sortie au cinéma est programmée pour le 21 octobre prochain. Il s'agit là du premier film d'horreur du studio, et à en juger par ces images le long-métrage de James Watkins (Speak No Evil) ne va pas faire dans la dentelle.
Gueule d'Argile sur le devant de la scène
Après deux films plutôt similaires dans leur forme (Superman et Supergirl), le DCU de James Gunn s'apprête à faire un pas de côté avec Clayface, film centré sur le personnage de Gueule d'Argile, un méchant de l'univers de Batman.
Ce long-métrage marque en effet la première incursion de DC Studios dans le genre de l'horreur et si Warner Bros. décrit Clayface comme un thriller horrifique, sa bande-annonce laisse à penser que le film va surtout faire la part belle au sous-genre inconfortable à regarder du "body horror."
Clayface suit Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), dont l'ascension fulgurante de "gamin des rues de Gotham à star hollywoodienne est brutalement interrompue lorsqu'un baron du crime le laisse atrocement défiguré," explique le synopsis officiel.
"Abandonné de tous et n'ayant plus rien à perdre, Matt se tourne vers un traitement expérimental qui lui rend miraculeusement son apparence... mais altère profondément sa perception de la réalité. Il sombre alors dans une spirale destructrice, consumé par un irrépressible désir de vengeance."
Le casting du film est complété par Naomie Ackie (Mickey 17), David Dencik (Star City), Eddie Marsan (Heartstopper), Max Minghella (The Handmaid's Tale) ou encore Ruby Sear (The Gentlemen), Nancy Carroll (The Crown) et Joshua James (Andor).
Clayface à la particularité d'être co-écrit par le nouveau maître de l'horreur, Mike Flanagan (The Haunting of Hill House, Carrie). Son co-scénariste est Hossein Amini, qui a déjà travaillé avec Watkins sur la série McMafia.
